packages.name: markdown
packages.synopsis: Package markdown is a standard-library-only CommonMark 0.31.2 parser and HTML renderer, in the spirit of markdown-it.
packages.doc:
Package markdown is a standard-library-only CommonMark 0.31.2 parser and HTML renderer, in the spirit of markdown-it. # Overview Rendering is a two-phase process, the same one the CommonMark reference parsers use. The block phase walks the input line by line, matching the continuation prefixes of the currently open container blocks (block quotes, list items), trying new block starts, and buffering leaf-block text. The inline phase then re-scans each paragraph and heading, resolving code spans, links, images, autolinks, raw HTML, character references, and — with the delimiter-stack algorithm from the specification appendix — emphasis and strong emphasis. There are no third-party dependencies and no cgo. # Rendering The package-level helpers use CommonMark-strict settings: html := markdown.Render("# Title\n\nSome *emphasis*.\n") err := markdown.RenderTo(os.Stdout, src) The output is an HTML fragment, not a whole document: no , or wrapper is generated. # Options New returns a reusable, concurrency-safe renderer: md := markdown.New(markdown.Options{ HTML: true, // pass raw HTML through (CommonMark default) Typographer: true, // smart quotes, en/em dashes, ellipses LineBreaks: true, // soft breaks become
LinkTarget: "_blank", }) html := md.Render(src) DefaultOptions reports the configuration the package-level functions use: Options{HTML: true}. With HTML set to false, raw HTML blocks and inline tags are escaped rather than passed through. # The AST Parse exposes the document tree, which Node.Walk traverses: doc := markdown.Parse(src) doc.Walk(func(n *markdown.Node) bool { if n.Type == markdown.Link { fmt.Println(n.Destination) } return true }) NodeType names the eighteen CommonMark node kinds; NodeType.IsBlock distinguishes block-level from inline nodes. Which Node fields carry meaning depends on the node type — see the Node documentation. # Conformance Every one of the 652 examples in the CommonMark 0.31.2 specification renders byte for byte identically to the reference output, including tab expansion to four-column tab stops, the left- and right-flanking delimiter run rules, link reference label case folding (full Unicode folding, so that "ẞ" and "SS" name the same reference), percent-encoding of link destinations, and the full WHATWG HTML5 named character reference table. # Security Rendering untrusted Markdown produces untrusted HTML. Two defences are built in, and one deliberate hole is left open: - Link destinations and image sources are sanitized by ValidateLink, the Go form of markdown-it's md.validateLink. The javascript:, vbscript:, file: and data: schemes are rejected — data: only for the inert data:image/{gif,png,jpeg,webp} payloads — and a rejected destination is replaced with the empty string. Matching is case-insensitive and ignores ASCII control characters, so "JaVaScRiPt:", " javascript:" and "java\tscript:" are all caught, as is "javascript:" (character references in a destination are decoded before validation). Sanitizing happens at parse time, so the destinations on the Parse AST are already safe. Options.ValidateLink replaces the policy. - Text, attribute values (title, alt, the info string's language class, LinkTarget) and URL destinations are escaped so nothing in the document can break out of the attribute it lands in. - Options.HTML, when true, passes raw HTML blocks and inline tags through verbatim. That is what CommonMark requires and it is what the package-level Render does, but it means a document can emit any HTML it likes — including

vars.doc:
ErrMarkdown is the root sentinel for every error returned by this package.
Every other sentinel wraps it, so errors.Is(err, ErrMarkdown) matches any
error originating here.

vars.signature: var ErrWrite = fmt.Errorf("%w: write output", ErrMarkdown)
vars.doc:
ErrWrite indicates that writing rendered output to an io.Writer failed. The
underlying writer error is wrapped alongside it, so both
errors.Is(err, markdown.ErrWrite) and errors.Is(err, io.ErrShortWrite) (for
example) can succeed.

types.name: Markdown
types.doc:
Markdown is a reusable, configured CommonMark renderer. A Markdown value is
safe for concurrent use by multiple goroutines.

funcs.name: New
funcs.doc: New returns a renderer configured by opts.

methods.name: Parse
methods.doc: Parse returns the CommonMark AST of src, using the renderer's options.

methods.name: Render
methods.doc:
Render converts CommonMark source to an HTML fragment using the renderer's
options.

methods.name: RenderTo
methods.signature: func (m *Markdown) RenderTo(w io.Writer, src string) error
methods.doc:
RenderTo writes the HTML rendering of src to w. Any error returned by w is
wrapped and can be tested with errors.Is against [ErrWrite].

types.name: Node
types.signature:
type Node struct {
	Type        NodeType
	Literal     string
	Level       int    // heading level, or ordered-list start number
	Destination string // link/image target
	Title       string
	Info        string // fenced code info string, or list kind
	Tight       bool   // list tightness
	Children    []*Node
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
types.doc:
Node is a node in the CommonMark AST.

Which fields carry meaning depends on Type:

	Heading      Level is 1-6.
	List         Info is "bullet" or "ordered", Literal is the bullet or
	             delimiter character ("-", "*", "+", "." or ")"), Level is
	             the start number of an ordered list, Tight reports list
	             tightness.
	Item         Literal and Info mirror the parent list's fields.
	CodeBlock    Literal is the code, Info the fenced info string (empty for
	             indented code blocks).
	HTMLBlock    Literal is the raw HTML.
	Text, Code,
	HTMLInline   Literal is the content.
	Link, Image  Destination and Title hold the target and title.

Children holds the child nodes in document order.

funcs.name: Parse
funcs.doc:
Parse returns the document AST for src, using the CommonMark-strict
defaults. The returned [Node] always has Type [Document].

methods.name: AppendChild
methods.doc: AppendChild appends c to n's children and records n as its parent.

methods.name: FirstChild
methods.doc: FirstChild returns n's first child, or nil when n has no children.

methods.name: LastChild
methods.doc: LastChild returns n's last child, or nil when n has no children.

methods.name: Parent
methods.doc:
Parent returns n's parent node, or nil for the document root and for nodes
that are not attached to a tree.

methods.name: Walk
methods.doc:
Walk calls fn for n and, depth first, for every descendant of n. Returning
false from fn skips that node's children.

types.name: NodeType
types.doc: NodeType identifies the kind of a [Node] in the CommonMark AST.

methods.name: IsBlock
methods.doc:
IsBlock reports whether the node type is a block-level (container or leaf
block) type rather than an inline type.

methods.name: String
methods.doc:
String returns the CommonMark name of the node type, for example "paragraph"
or "block_quote". Unknown values render as "NodeType(n)".

types.name: Options
types.doc:
Options configures a Markdown renderer.

The zero value is not the CommonMark default: [Render] and [RenderTo] use
Options{HTML: true}, which is CommonMark-strict. Construct a renderer with
[New] to change any of these.

funcs.name: DefaultOptions
funcs.doc:
DefaultOptions returns the CommonMark-strict configuration used by the
package-level [Render] and [RenderTo]: raw HTML enabled, everything else
disabled.

funcs.name: Render
funcs.doc:
Render converts CommonMark source to an HTML fragment using the
CommonMark-strict defaults (raw HTML enabled, no typographic
substitutions, soft breaks preserved as newlines).

funcs.name: RenderTo
funcs.signature: func RenderTo(w io.Writer, src string) error
funcs.doc:
RenderTo writes the HTML rendering of src to w using the CommonMark-strict
defaults. Errors from w are wrapped and can be tested with errors.Is against
[ErrWrite].

funcs.name: ValidateLink
funcs.doc:
ValidateLink reports whether url may be emitted as a link destination or an
image source.

It is the Go form of markdown-it's default md.validateLink. Destinations
using the javascript:, vbscript:, file: or data: schemes are rejected, with
the single exception of the four inert data:image/... subtypes (gif, png,
jpeg, webp) that cannot carry script. Everything else — including relative
URLs, fragments and unknown schemes — is allowed.

The scheme is matched case-insensitively, and ASCII control characters and
spaces are removed before matching, so JaVaScRiPt:, " javascript:" and
"java\tscript:" are all rejected. (Browsers strip tabs and newlines from a
URL before resolving its scheme, so a renderer must too; this is stricter
than markdown-it, which only trims the ends of the string.)

A destination that fails validation is not dropped: the link or image is
still produced, with an empty destination, which is also what markdown-it
does.

Override it per renderer with [Options].ValidateLink — for example
`func(string) bool { return true }` to disable sanitizing entirely, in a
context where the input is already trusted.

examples.name: Render
RenderTo
ValidateLink
examples.doc:
Link destinations using an executable scheme are sanitized by default, the
way markdown-it's validateLink does it: the link is still rendered, with an
empty destination.
